subject: Proposal: rolling-weighted-epoch aggregation for p50/p95 during burst traffic
messages:
From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Alvarez <natalie@brightlinehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-07T09:15:00-07:00
Subject: Proposal: rolling-weighted-epoch aggregation for p50/p95 during burst traffic

Hi Natalie / Brightline procurement team —

Following our call yesterday I pulled together a compact proposal for how Redwood can handle short, sharp bursts without triggering a p95 contract exception for hosted API customers. High-level idea: compute p50/p95 on a rolling-weighted-epoch rather than a single long sliding window, so recent burst samples carry more weight but short spikes don’t immediately push the long-term percentile over the threshold. This preserves user-facing latency guarantees while making evidence for short incidents easier to reason about.

What I attached: rolling-weighted-epoch-proposal-v1.pdf (high level + pseudocode). Also proposing we capture a small evidence export schema (see later message) for any exception request.

Key points / ask:
- Measurement: primary SLOs remain p50/p95 per region/model. We propose a 1-hour rolling epoch composed of 12 five-minute buckets. Each bucket contributes to the rolling measurement with an exponential weight (newer buckets weight more).
- Burst carveout: if a contiguous set of buckets shows >3x baseline qps and median latency increase > 50ms we mark that episode as a candidate for an "operational burst" record rather than immediate SLA breach.
- Evidence: export must include timestamp, region, model_id, request_size, routed_pool, and per-request latency. We included an evidence-schema.csv as a suggested minimal schema.
- Fallbacks: recommend automatic regional spill to Dedicated pool for a configurable grace window (default 120s) during sustained bursts.

Next steps I propose:
1) Can Brightline confirm whether the 1-hour epoch / 12x5min buckets are acceptable?
2) If accepted, we schedule a short stress test (30-90 min) next week with Redwood capturing evidence and producing a sample exception packet for you to review.
3) Procurement: if you want this behavior codified in the SLO addendum (rolling-weighted handling and evidence requirements), we can draft language.

Attachments: rolling-weighted-epoch-proposal-v1.pdf (proposal + pseudocode)

Thanks,
Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Mobile: +1 (415) 555-0192

From: Natalie Alvarez <natalie@brightlinehealth.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
Cc: Procurement Team <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-07T13:42:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling-weighted-epoch aggregation for p50/p95 during burst traffic

Thanks Diego — this is helpful and thoughtful. A few clarifying questions before we commit to a test: 

1) For contract language: Brightline’s legal will want a concise definition of what counts as a "candidate operational burst" vs an SLA failure. Can you provide a one-paragraph definition we can share internally?

2) Measurement windows: Why 12x5min buckets (versus, say, 6x10min)? Is the 5-minute granularity required for the weighting math or mainly to capture burst shape?

3) Evidence schema: procurement would like the export to include request_id and a hash of the prompt (for sampling verification). Also please confirm retention window for evidence (we need at least 90 days).

4) If we run a stress test, will Redwood sign off on the packet as authoritative for the exception request, or will Brightline expect a third-party audit?

If you can answer the above and share the one-paragraph definition, we can route this to procurement/legal quickly.

Best,
Natalie Alvarez
Director of Product Ops, Brightline Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Cc: Natalie Alvarez <natalie@brightlinehealth.com>
Date: 2025-09-08T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling-weighted-epoch aggregation for p50/p95 during burst traffic

Diego — good framing. Two quick items from an ops/contract perspective: 

- One-paragraph definition (suggested): "An 'operational burst' is a contiguous episode where traffic to a given regional model increases beyond three times the historical baseline (30-day rolling median) for at least two consecutive 5-minute buckets and is accompanied by a median latency increase exceeding 50ms. Episodes identified as operational bursts will be treated as candidates for temporary operational carveouts and evaluated against the evidence packet prior to any SLA credit or remediation." Feel free to edit.

- Granularity: 5-minute buckets are preferable because they let us detect short sharp spikes and attribute routing/fallback behavior precisely. 10-minute buckets smooth too aggressively and make short incidents look bigger in aggregate. So I'd push for 12x5min for the 1-hour epoch.

- Evidence retention: agree to 90 days as a minimum; ops will need to know if Brightline requires longer for audit (if so we'll escalate to infra).

- Canary & remediation: recommend we add an explicit canary phase to the stress test where we run a synthetic burst against a mirrored routing path for 15 minutes, confirm the rolling-weighted outputs match the expected signals, then run a 60-minute production-like stress with live traffic shaping off. Also add a fallback to dedicated routing and a circuit-breaker that re-routes >=30% of traffic after 90s if latency remains bad.

Happy to be the internal lead — Diego, if you want, I can draft a short addendum paragraph to insert in the SLO appendix after the stress test.

Marissa Cole
Head of Customer Reliability | Redwood Inference

From: Diego Fernandez <diego_fernandez@redwood.com>
To: Natalie Alvarez <natalie@brightlinehealth.com>, Procurement Team <procurement@brightlinehealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
Date: 2025-09-09T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Proposal: rolling-weighted-epoch aggregation for p50/p95 during burst traffic

Thanks Natalie / Marissa — appreciate the quick turnaround. Summary and agreed next steps: 

1) Definition: we will adopt Marissa's suggested one-paragraph definition (below) as the working definition for the stress test and the draft SLO addendum.

2) Measurement window: we proceed with 1-hour rolling epoch comprised of 12x5min buckets (newer buckets exponential weight). Karthik / infra will include code to compute both 12x5min and a 6x10min view for our internal validation but contract will reference 12x5min.

3) Evidence & retention: we'll include request_id and prompt_hash in the evidence export; retention set to 90 days by default (we'll note this in the draft addendum). Evidence packet will be the authoritative record for the exception request. If Brightline requires an independent audit we can coordinate but it is not required to evaluate a candidate burst.

4) Canary & stress test plan: Proposed timeline:
   - Wed 2025-09-17: 15-minute mirrored canary burst (off-peak) -> internal validation
   - Thurs 2025-09-18: 60-minute staged stress with evidence capture and fallback exercised

5) Procurement asks: please confirm whether you want the rolling-weighted behavior codified in the SLO addendum or handled as an operational playbook. We can prepare a one-paragraph SLO addendum and a separate playbook appendix.

Attachments: evidence-schema.csv (minimal export columns + sample rows)

If that all looks good I'll book the canary and include Marissa/Karthik on the runbook and test plan.

Diego Fernandez
Senior Solutions Engineer | Redwood Inference
Phone: +1 (415) 555-0192
